title: Trans-Saharan Trade Routes (c. 500-1500 CE)
key_facts: Vast network of trade routes crossing Sahara Desert
Connected Mediterranean world with sub-Saharan Africa
Major commodities: gold, salt, ivory, slaves, textiles
Facilitated spread of Islam and cultural exchange
causes: Demand for West African gold in Mediterranean markets
Need for salt in sub-Saharan Africa (vital for preservation)
Development of camel caravans enabling desert crossing
Islamic expansion creating unified commercial networks
outcome: Rise of powerful West African empires (Ghana, Mali, Songhai)
Spread of Islam throughout West Africa
Urban development of trading cities like Timbuktu and Gao
Cultural and intellectual exchange across continents

figures.name: Mansa Musa
figures.role: Mali ruler whose pilgrimage showcased wealth

impacts: Economic foundation for West African empires' power
Islamic scholarship and learning centers in desert cities
Cultural exchange between Africa, Europe, and Middle East
Established trade patterns that lasted until colonial period
